floorByAgentClass.description: Per-agent-class first-request floor: median (n/min/p10/mean) of each measured agent's first transcript request only (uncachedInput + cacheWrite + cacheRead, before any tool use) -- the same definition agentContextFloor.measuredFloor uses, broken out per agentClass instead of a single whole-corpus figure.
floorByAgentClass.source: this phase's own regenerateCommand (see methodology.regenerateCommand), re-run against the existing on-disk corpus -- no fresh dispatch; every record counted predates this phase's own code change
floorByAgentClass.zeroValueNote: 6 records in this regeneration have firstRequestTokens === 0 (contributing the minTokens: 0 seen on estimate/plan/refute below) -- the same count as, and consistent with, agentContextFloor's already-documented 'excluding 6 agents with a tokens value of exactly 0 - orphaned zero-usage transcript entries, not real observations'. This addendum does NOT apply that exclusion -- it counts every record with a non-null firstRequestTokens, including zero-valued ones -- because the approved scope of this phase excludes only cached/sidecarOnly (null) records, not zero-valued measured ones; a future phase revisiting this exclusion should treat it as a methodology decision, not a bug.
floorByAgentClass.populationCaveat: The corpus grew between phase 2's measurement (runSet.included: 40 runs / 1943 records) and this regeneration (44 runs / 2110 records) -- this is corpus growth between measurements, not a re-baseline; runSet/byAgentClass/agentContextFloor above remain byte-unchanged from phase 2. Summing n across every class below gives 2086, a 24-record gap against this regeneration's own recordCount of 2110 -- consistent with the 23-record gap phase 2 already noted between agentContextFloor.measuredFloor.n (1920) and runSet.included.totalAgentRecords (1943); in both cases the gap is exactly the count of cached/sidecarOnly records excluded from the floor population, not an error.

mixedBucketCaveat.estimate: Mixes mechanical (estimate:list/write:*/tier:*) and judgment (estimate:rate:*) sub-labels under one agentClass bucket, because agentClassFromLabel groups purely on the string before the first colon -- this figure must NOT be read as a clean mechanical-only floor.
mixedBucketCaveat.act: Mixes mechanical (act:round-note:*, irreducible per docs/mechanical-agent-inventory.md) and judgment (act:code, act:<kind>:<ident>) sub-labels under the same one-bucket-per-colon-split rule -- this figure must NOT be read as a clean mechanical-only floor either, mirroring the estimate caveat above.

mechanicalContextTrim.description: Comparison point for the mechanical-agent context trim (agentType / effort), plus the measured size of the trim itself. preChangeMedianTokens below PINS the pre-change side of the eventual lane comparison so a later run cannot silently re-baseline it. No post-change LANE corpus exists (no agent() call site was edited), but the per-agent effect of agentType and of CLAUDE.md was measured directly -- see measuredTrim2x2.
mechanicalContextTrim.status: agentType CONFIRMED resolving from the Workflow runtime and THREADED at the local-only mechanical sites; Workflow-path trim MEASURED at 8907 tokens/agent (-23%), roughly half the 19894 the claude -p 2x2 predicted
mechanicalContextTrim.statusReason: The phase is feasibility-gated on a spike (.claude/workflows/spike-agent-type.js). It HAS NOW BEEN RUN via the Workflow tool -- run wf_2bea58b9-38f (8 cases, 5 OK / 3 threw) plus follow-up probe wf_6cca94eb-de0 -- and its result is recorded under workflowPathSpike below. ONE HALF OF THAT RUN IS INVALID AND ITS APPARENT FINDING IS RETRACTED. (1) The agentType cases raised `agent type not found`, but for a documented DISPATCHING-SIDE setup reason, not a runtime limitation: the run was dispatched from a session whose project root had no .claude/agents/ directory at session start, and the definition was copied in mid-run. Claude Code's subagent docs state the watcher covers only directories that existed when the session started, so creating a scope's first agent file in a NEW agents directory requires a restart. Those cases measured that mistake. agentType Workflow-path resolution is therefore UNVERIFIED, exactly as it was before the run -- it is NOT a measured negative, and the earlier claim that the trim is 'undeliverable' was wrong and is withdrawn. (2) effort:'low' passed to agent() IS honored (see effortDecision), reversing the definition-side negative; that result is sound and unaffected. The context-floor figures in measuredTrim2x2 are likewise unaffected: they come from a controlled 2x2 over `claude -p` sessions, which resolve the .claude/agents/ registry successfully and record the SAME per-request usage that scripts/lib/token-report.mjs reads. agentType: 'rdm-mechanical' IS now threaded at the mechanical call sites of the four local-only workflows (19 records; see threadedSites), on the strength of the documented registry behaviour plus the measured --agent resolution, with the confirming Workflow dispatch still outstanding. No FRESH lane run has been dispatched since, so there is still no post-change LANE corpus and no floorByAgentClass delta to report -- the delta must be measured per measurementProtocolForTheFollowUp before any saving is claimed. See docs/workflow-schemas.md § 'agentType / effort options spike' for the full evidence tables and the disposition.

workflowPathSpike.description: The live Workflow-tool dispatch of .claude/workflows/spike-agent-type.js. This is the call path the actual call sites use, so where it disagrees with the `claude -p` measurement it governs.
workflowPathSpike.agentTypeResolutionStatus: UNVERIFIED -- the cases that tested it are INVALID and their apparent negative is RETRACTED. Do not record this as false.
workflowPathSpike.agentTypeEvidence: RETRACTED. Cases B ('rdm-mechanical') and F ('rdm-mechanical' + effort) threw `agent({agentType}): agent type 'rdm-mechanical' not found. Available agents: claude, claude-code-guide, Explore, general-purpose, Plan, statusline-setup`, and probe wf_6cca94eb-de0 reproduced it. This was first written up as a measured negative. It is not one. The run was dispatched from a session rooted at the main checkout, whose project root had NO .claude/agents/ directory at session start; the operator created that directory and copied the definition in mid-session, then dispatched. Claude Code's subagent documentation names this as a restart case: the watcher 'covers only directories that existed when the session started, so after creating a scope's first agent file in a new agents directory, restart to load it.' The definition was therefore never loaded, and the retry probe re-tested the same unwatched directory rather than demonstrating a non-refreshing registry. The docs further note project subagents are discovered by walking up from the CWD, so the worktree's own committed .claude/agents/ was never in scope for a session rooted elsewhere. Cases B/F say nothing about agent({agentType}).
workflowPathSpike.agentTypeFailureModeNote: This part STANDS, on case C alone -- a deliberately unknown id ('no-such-agent-xyz'), which does not depend on the registry containing our definition and is the case designed to test exactly this. Previously INFERRED from a runtime string table, now observed. The spike script distinguishes a throw from a null return explicitly, so the shape is unambiguous. Contrast an unknown `model` id, which resolves agent() to null silently.
workflowPathSpike.hypothesesResolved: The earlier H1 ('a Workflow run never consults a project-local .claude/agents/') is RULED OUT by the documentation: the directory is consulted, and watched live once it exists at session start. H1/H2 was a false dilemma produced by the invalid test, and neither is a finding of this run.
workflowPathSpike.whatWouldCloseIt: One dispatch of spike-agent-type.js from a session whose project root contains .claude/agents/rdm-mechanical.md AT SESSION START -- which any ordinary session in this repo satisfies once this branch lands, since the definition sits at the repo root. Read case B's toolNames: a trimmed list is the positive evidence AC4 gates on.
workflowPathSpike.scopeConsequence: NONE -- withdrawn. The earlier claim that this 'removes the local-only-vs-distributed distinction' rested on the retracted finding. The distribution blocker (no .claude/agents/ emission surface downstream) is unaffected and still stands on its own.
workflowPathSpike.firstRequestTokensNote: Identical across all 5 OK cases, which is expected: every one ran as the DEFAULT agent because no agentType ever resolved. The run therefore yields NO Workflow-path floor measurement, and measuredTrim2x2 remains the only floor evidence. Not comparable to the 2x2 cells -- different prompt, different session.
workflowPathSpike.structuredReturnNote: The follow-up task's scope item 3 (does agent(prompt,{schema}) still work under `tools: Bash, StructuredOutput`, and is agentType honored through parallel()) could NOT be exercised, because nothing resolved.

threadedSites.description: Mechanical agent() call sites now passing agentType: 'rdm-mechanical'. Written as a plain literal at each site, never a module-level constant, because the source text is byte-copied across files with different scopes.
threadedSites.notThreaded: The three DISTRIBUTED workflows (autopilot.js, dispatch-phase.js, review-refute-fix.js) -- blocked by the missing emission surface -- and every JUDGMENT site (find:*, refute:*, plan:*, implement:*, synthesize:draft, analyze:*, estimate:rate:*, plan-review's act:*).
threadedSites.gate: scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh §2c asserts both directions with planted-mutation self-tests, plus a completeness sweep that fails if a site is added or removed without updating the asserted list, or if any agentType other than 'rdm-mechanical' appears.
threadedSites.residualRisk: Workflow-path resolution is unconfirmed (see workflowPathSpike). If it does not resolve, these four workflows RAISE on first dispatch rather than degrading silently -- a loud failure, not a corrupting one.
threadedSites.expectedSavingBasis: workflowPathTrimMeasured.controlledPair -- MEASURED on the Workflow path these sites use, and corroborated by a live backlog dispatch (laneDelta, ~19-20% per class at n=1). The earlier 19894 from measuredTrim2x2 measured the CLI --agent path and overstates these sites by 2.23x.

workflowPathTrimMeasured.description: The Workflow-path measurement of the agentType trim, taken after a session restart rooted in this worktree so .claude/agents/ was present at session start. THIS IS THE GOVERNING FIGURE for the threaded call sites: it measures the same call path they use. measuredTrim2x2 below measures the CLI --agent path and predicts roughly TWICE this saving -- see predictionError.
workflowPathTrimMeasured.resolutionEvidence: Spike case B resolved and reported toolNames ['Bash','StructuredOutput'] against the control's nine, so the definition loaded AND its tool restriction is enforced. Case C (unknown id) now enumerates 'rdm-mechanical' in its Available-agents list. The live backlog lane's agent sidecars record {'agentType':'rdm-mechanical','model':'haiku'} -- which also confirms a per-call model pin still overrides the definition, the assumption behind omitting model: from the agent file.

controlledPair.description: Spike cases A and B: same session, identical prompt, dispatched back-to-back. firstRequestTokens = input + cache_creation + cache_read on the first assistant record.
controlledPair.replication: Cases E and F repeat the pair with effort:'low' added to both sides and reproduce it EXACTLY: 38689 -> 29782, the same 8907. All five default-agent cases (A,D,E,G,H) measured exactly 38689; both agentType cases (B,F) exactly 29782.

laneDelta.description: The first post-change lane dispatch: `backlog` (propose-only, verified zero-mutation -- rdm status and git worktree both clean afterwards). Compared against the PINNED preChangeMedianTokens for the same agent classes, which is the only legal basis.
laneDelta.caveats: n=1 per class -- DIRECTIONAL, not a re-baseline. Do NOT overwrite preChangeMedianTokens with these. Not perfectly like-for-like either: model:mechanical runs unpinned on opus (it is the bootstrap that RESOLVES the tier), fetch:report on haiku, while the pinned medians aggregate mixed models over different prompts. Both classes nonetheless drop ~19-20%, consistent with the controlled 23%.

predictionError.explanation: Both ends of the comparison compress on the Workflow path. A Workflow subagent's DEFAULT floor is much cheaper than a CLI session's (38689 vs 47084) -- fewer tools, no skill listing, leaner harness -- while the TRIMMED agent is slightly more expensive (29782 vs 27190). The margin between them therefore roughly halves. The claude -p 2x2 remains internally valid; it simply measures a different call path than the call sites use.
predictionError.lesson: This is precisely what AC5 exists to catch: the per-agent figure was recorded as a prediction and labelled as such everywhere, and measuring it on the real path cut it by more than half. Never quote measuredTrim2x2's 19894 as the saving these call sites deliver.

measuredTrim2x2.description: Controlled 2x2, run live in this worktree on claude-opus-5, one identical trivial prompt per cell. Factor A: session default agent vs `claude --agent rdm-mechanical` (this repo's .claude/agents/ definition). Factor B: project CLAUDE.md present vs temporarily moved aside and restored. The user-global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md is present in all four cells and cancels out of every difference.
measuredTrim2x2.metric: firstRequestTokens = input + cache_creation + cache_read on the session's first assistant record -- the same quantity buildRecords computes per agent, so it is directly comparable to floorByAgentClass. Cache-placement-independent by construction.

agentTypeTrimTokens.note: The two margins agree to within 11 tokens (0.06%), so the agentType effect and the CLAUDE.md effect are independent and additive. This is the whole prize on offer: the default agent's system prompt plus the tool schemas of every tool rdm-mechanical does not receive.

claudeMdCostTokens.note: Equal to within 11 tokens: a custom agentType pays the FULL project-memory cost. A trimmed system prompt and a two-tool allowlist displace none of it.

claudeMdFinding.implicationForAttribution: agentContextFloor.attribution uses chars/4 and is left UNCHANGED as the recorded phase-2 figure, but it is now known to understate this file by 60%. At the measured 2.49 chars/token, claudeMdSubtotal's 61247 chars price at roughly 24600 tokens rather than 15312, and remainderToolSchemasSystemPrompt (23526) is overstated by the same amount since it is derived as floor minus that subtotal.
claudeMdFinding.avoidabilityEvidence: The runtime's agent-definition frontmatter schema accepts description, tools, disallowedTools, prompt, model, effort, permissionMode, mcpServers, hooks, maxTurns, color, background, memory, isolation, observer, observerMessage, observeSubagents -- none suppresses CLAUDE.md. `memory` is E.enum(["user","project","local"]) scoping auto-loading of ~/.claude/agent-memory/ files, i.e. it ADDS context. The only suppression switches are process-global: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_MDS, and --bare / CLAUDE_CODE_SIMPLE=1 (which also strips hooks, LSP and auth).
claudeMdFinding.disposition: Per the phase body: recorded as a finding, and not pursued further. No CLAUDE.md restructuring was attempted or is proposed. The measurement only reprices the option -- a hypothetical 30% CLAUDE.md reduction would be worth ~5800 tokens per agent, not the ~3600 the chars/4 estimate implied.

corroborationCrossProject.description: Independent corroboration from the existing on-disk corpus: per-agent-class median firstRequestTokens grouped by project slug, for two repos whose CLAUDE.md files differ by 31144 chars (rdm 48207, bowling-app 17063) and which share the same user-global copy.
corroborationCrossProject.caveat: CORROBORATING ONLY. The two repos differ in skills, hooks and prompt sizes as well as CLAUDE.md, so this cannot isolate CLAUDE.md the way measuredTrim2x2 does. It is reported because it reproduces the same 'chars/4 understates by roughly half again' signature from an entirely different dataset.

mechanicalContextTrim.preChangeBasis: floorByAgentClass.byClass above, verbatim -- the per-class medianTokens recorded by the add-per-agent-class-floor phase over the 44-run / 2110-record on-disk corpus. These are the ONLY figures the eventual before/after claim may use.

excludedFromAnyMechanicalClaim.estimate: mixed bucket -- see floorByAgentClass.mixedBucketCaveat.estimate; contains the judgment estimate:rate:* alongside estimate:list/write:*/tier:*

mechanicalContextTrim.mustNotCompareAgainst: agentContextFloor.measuredFloor.reportedFloorTokens (38837.5) and agentContextFloor.legacyRegression.interceptTokens (37552) -- both are WHOLE-CORPUS figures, not per-class ones; comparing a mechanical-class median against either measures corpus composition, not the change.
mechanicalContextTrim.measurementProtocolForTheFollowUp: Scope the fresh run with --since <ISO date of the first post-change run> so the pre-change corpus is not averaged in: `node scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs --format json --since <date> --workflow autopilot --workflow dispatch-phase --workflow plan-review --workflow backlog --workflow estimate --workflow document`, then read report.floorByAgentClass. A single fresh dispatch yields single-digit n per class, so the resulting delta is DIRECTIONAL, not a re-baseline -- record n per class alongside it and do not overwrite the figures above.
mechanicalContextTrim.effortDecision: NOT applied at any call site -- but as of the Workflow-path run the reason is SCOPE, not inertness. The two routes were measured separately and they DISAGREE. Route 1, definition-side (effort:"low" in the agent frontmatter, via --agents, whose zod schema carries effort: E.union([E.enum(vO), E.number().int()]).optional()): the agent resolved, ran normally, and its first assistant record still said effort:"high" -- accepted, not honored. Route 2, call-site (agent(prompt, {effort:'low'}) from inside a Workflow run, spike case E): the transcript recorded effort:"low" -- HONORED. Against the fixed control (across 6290 transcripts / 156384 assistant records the top-level `effort` field holds only "high" (55945) or is absent (100439), and "low" ZERO times) a single "low" record is conclusive, and case E is that record; the four sibling cases in the same run all recorded "high". Case H additionally shows an INVALID effort value is accepted and silently degrades to "high" rather than throwing -- the opposite of agentType, where a bad value takes the lane down. scripts/verify-workflow-review.sh §2b still fails if any workflow script passes effort:, now because the phase body forbids threading it (step 4, written on the strength of the definition-side negative that route 2 overturned), not because the option is inert. Flipping that gated invariant across ~15 call sites is a scope decision for the roadmap owner. Carried by task finish-agent-type-effort-spike-and-thread-mechanical-sites scope item 5, which is now live and unblocked. Limits on the positive: n=1 per cell, and the run measured only that the request RAN at low -- not whether low effort degrades mechanical transcription fidelity, which the follow-up must establish before shipping it.

confounds: roadmap size - a roadmap with more phases dispatches more dispatch-phase/plan-review/estimate agent invocations inside a single autopilot run; larger roadmap does not imply a more expensive phase
phase difficulty / model tier - rdm-estimate assigns each phase a difficulty and model tier; a high-tier phase's agents run on a more expensive model and do not necessarily use fewer tokens for it

rework rounds - a phase that bounces through plan-review or code-review rework re-runs find/refute/plan/implement agents multiple times; its total is not comparable to a phase that passed on the first pass

user-specific CLAUDE.md - the user-global CLAUDE.md measured for the context floor is this operator's own machine; a different operator's global instructions file will shift the floor by a different amount

model-identity drift - some agent records carry a generic alias (haiku, sonnet) rather than a resolved snapshot ID and contribute zero measurable usage; per-model comparisons must key on the exact snapshot ID
run completeness - 3 of 19 autopilot runs in scope are killed and 4 are failed (0 agents)
comparableUnit: per-agent-class figures and per-phase-dispatch figures; raw per-run totals are not a valid comparison unit for later phases' before/after claims

noBehaviorChange.statement: measurement and documentation only; no file under .claude/workflows/, .claude/workflows/lib/, .claude/skills/, scripts/measure-lane-tokens.mjs, or scripts/lib/token-report.mjs was modified by this phase's commit

nonGatingRefutationSkip.description: Refuter spend broken out by the SEVERITY of the finding each refuter graded — the dimension byAgentClass['refute'] cannot see. This is the evidence behind the phase-6 change: the review pipeline no longer spawns a refuter for a `suggestion`, because `suggestion` gates nothing at any tier (hasBlocking's blocker set is ['blocking'], widened to ['blocking','concern'] at the `large` tier, and the AC table is a separate structured channel that never reads finding severity).
nonGatingRefutationSkip.method: Each refuter's transcript opens with the prompt it was given, and refutePrompt embeds the whole finding as pretty-printed JSON; the forced StructuredOutput tool call carries its verdict. The finding is extracted by brace-matching the object whose closing brace abuts the 'Start from the stance:' sentinel, so a context.target that itself contains braces (the --implementation-plan shape) parses correctly. Usage is the same requestId-deduped, four-class join buildRecords performs for the baseline above.

measurementWindow.why: Pins the run set so a later lane run cannot silently re-baseline these committed figures. --check re-applies this window unless --until overrides it.
measurementWindow.note: This window is WIDER than the runSet section above (40 runs / 1943 agent records, measured 2026-07-26): the corpus grew between the two measurements. These rows are therefore NOT subtractable against byAgentClass above — compare them only within this section.

nonGatingRefutationSkip.caveat: No post-change lane corpus exists — every run in the window executed pre-change code. The projected drop is measured over the HISTORICAL corpus (the refuters this change would not have spawned, priced at their own real recorded usage), not claimed from a fresh run. Confirm on the next real lane run with the regenerateCommand above: the `suggestion` row should go to zero agents.

gating.checkGatedBy: node scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs --check docs/token-baseline.json (recomputes over the real corpus; requires the sidecars, so it is run by hand, not by the harness)
gating.auditGatedBy: node scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs --audit docs/token-baseline.json, run by scripts/verify-token-report.sh section 6 — corpus-free arithmetic audit (rows sum to refuteTotals, projected re-derives from the rows, every refutedRate is its own quotient), so the committed figures are gated on any machine.

nonGatingRefutationSkip.decision: `concern` keeps its refuter. Over this window a concern is overturned MORE often than a blocking finding (50.4% of 522 graded vs 38.1% of 197), and it gates outright at the `large` tier, so its refuter is buying something. `suggestion` is overturned 74.2% of the time and gates nothing either way — the verdict changes no outcome, so the agent is pure cost. The pass-through set is therefore ['suggestion'] and is tier-independent, which is why no tier has to be threaded into the pipeline.

refuterFanout.description: Two descriptive distributions over the SAME refuter/finder corpus nonGatingRefutationSkip measures, extending scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs rather than adding a sibling instrument: (1) findings-per-finder, split by mode and dimension, sourced from each finder's OWN transcript output (its last StructuredOutput `findings` array), never inferred from how many refuters were dispatched — since workflow-token-reduction phase 6, a `suggestion` finding is never dispatched to a refuter at all, so refuter count is strictly less than finding count and cannot stand in for it; and (2) how many refuters a single review unit (one dispatch-phase code-review stage, one plan-review phase unit) dispatched, keyed by the unit identity embedded in each refuter's own initiating prompt turn.
refuterFanout.method: Both a refuter's dimension and its review-unit identity are resolved from the SAME header line of its prompt that nonGatingRefutationSkip already parses for severity (`A prior reviewer raised this <dim> finding against <target>:`), via a new extractRefuterContext() parser — never from the refuter's own `refute:<mode>:(f.id|dim.key:idx)` label, which a finder-supplied `f.id` (the common case) displaces the dimension out of entirely. The review-unit boundary is deliberately NOT `phaseTitle`/`phaseIndex`: those are the workflow's own declared pipeline stages, and in a plan-review run they are IDENTICAL across every review unit in the run — measured directly on run wf_55af7324-87c (`--roadmap project-agnostic-lane`): 152 agents, all 96 refuters sitting at the SAME phaseIndex across 9 distinct review units, which would silently collapse to "one unit with 96 refuters" under that key. `context.target` supplies the real boundary instead — a single-line bare `task/<slug>`/`<roadmap>/<stem>` in code mode (identity ends at the trailing `:` on the same line), or a multi-line `phase <roadmap>/<stem>\n\n<body>` in plan mode (identity is the first line, well before the `:` trailing the whole body). A target that is itself pretty-printed JSON (the --implementation-plan shape) or implausibly long is rejected rather than captured as a fake identity, and is reported as unrecoverable, never bucketed into an existing unit.

measurementWindow.why: Pins the run set so a later lane run cannot silently re-baseline these committed figures. --check re-applies this window unless --until overrides it. Regenerated in the SAME pass as nonGatingRefutationSkip above, over the identical window.
measurementWindow.note: This window is the SAME as nonGatingRefutationSkip's (both regenerated together), but is WIDER than the runSet section above (40 runs / 1943 agent records, measured 2026-07-26): the corpus grew between the two measurements. These rows are therefore NOT subtractable against byAgentClass above, and are a DIFFERENT measurement from nonGatingRefutationSkip's per-severity breakdown even though the windows happen to coincide here — a future regeneration of either section is not required to keep them aligned. Compare figures only within this section.

refuterFanout.caveat: No post-change lane corpus exists for the findings-per-finder distribution either — it reports what finders actually emitted over the historical corpus, not a forecast. The per-unit refuter-count distribution only recovers 64.6% of refuters to a unit (639/989); the remainder (chiefly --implementation-plan's raw-JSON-shaped target, and refuters with no transcript at all) are reported as unrecoverable and are never bucketed into any unit's count, so the distribution is a lower bound on true per-unit fan-out, not an exact accounting.

gating.checkGatedBy: node scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs --check docs/token-baseline.json (recomputes over the real corpus; requires the sidecars, so it is run by hand, not by the harness)
gating.auditGatedBy: node scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs --audit docs/token-baseline.json, run by scripts/verify-token-report.sh section 6 — corpus-free arithmetic audit (every row’s min <= p50 <= p90 <= max, recoveredRefuters + unrecoverableRefuterCount === totalRefuters, recoveryRatePercent re-derives), so the committed figures are gated on any machine.

determiningFindingRank.description: Where in a severity-then-confidence ranking does the finding that actually DETERMINED the outcome sit? A refutation budget that grades only the top N candidates is free iff that finding is almost always near the top, and sheds real signal iff the rank is spread out. Nothing else in the bound-review-fan-out roadmap answers this, and phase 4 may not choose an N without it. Measured by replaying the live pipeline's own rule (rankFindings / survives / hasBlocking, IMPORTED from .claude/workflows/lib/review.mjs, never reimplemented) over the historical sidecar corpus, reusing the SAME prompt-derived review-unit key refuterFanout above established.
determiningFindingRank.method: RANKED OVER THE CANDIDATE LIST, NOT THE SURVIVOR LIST. Ranking among survivors is degenerate: SEVERITY_RANK orders blocking(0) < concern(1) < suggestion(2), so the top-ranked SURVIVOR is by construction the one that makes hasBlocking true and the rank would be a constant 1 for every determining unit — a tautology, not a measurement. A refutation budget truncates the CANDIDATE list (what the finders emitted) before any of it is graded, so the candidate list is the ranking a cap would actually apply. Each unit's candidate list is assembled from its finders' OWN StructuredOutput `findings` arrays; each candidate's disposition comes from joining the refuter that graded it by (unit, prompt-derived dimension, finding id), falling back to a structural deep-equal of the finding JSON. The walk then takes rankFindings(candidates) in order and reports the 1-based index of the first candidate that both `survives` and `hasBlocking`. SEVERITY IS CHECKED BEFORE DISPOSITION, and that order is load-bearing: a candidate outside hasBlocking's blocker set for the tier being walked (a suggestion at either tier; a concern at the default tier) can never be the determining finding whatever its verdict turns out to be, so the walk skips it outright and neither its verdict nor a MISSING verdict can decide the unit. Checking disposition first would silently reclassify a genuinely non-determining unit — one blocking candidate that WAS refuted, plus a suggestion whose refuter transcript is unparseable — as unrecoverable, collapsing exactly the distinction this section exists to keep; and because this window predates workflow-token-reduction phase 6, when suggestions WERE still dispatched to refuters, such units really occur in it. The review-unit key is phase 1's, unchanged — the target embedded in each agent's own prompt, read on the refuter side by extractRefuterContext and on the FINDER side by a second reader, extractFinderContext, of the identical context.target that findPrompt writes as `Review target: <target>.`. Nothing anywhere in this measurement reads phaseTitle/phaseIndex.

measurementWindow.why: Pins the run set so a later lane run cannot silently re-baseline these committed figures. Derived from measure()'s already-filtered runFiles — the SAME filtered corpus refuterFanout and nonGatingRefutationSkip are built from — so all three sections describe one identical window and this one cannot re-baseline while the others stay pinned. --check re-applies the window recorded in nonGatingRefutationSkip unless --until overrides it.
measurementWindow.note: Identical to refuterFanout's window (all three sections are regenerated in one pass), and WIDER than the runSet section above (40 runs / 1943 agent records, measured 2026-07-26): the corpus grew between measurements. These figures are therefore NOT subtractable against byAgentClass. Compare only within this section.

determiningFindingRank.recoverabilityScoping: CONTAMINATION IS PER UNIT, NEVER RUN-WIDE. Every reason in the closed vocabulary above is decidable from the unit's OWN records. An agent whose unit identity does not resolve — chiefly the --implementation-plan target, which is itself pretty-printed JSON and is rejected by construction rather than captured as a fake identity — is attributable to NO unit, so it marks no unit unrecoverable; it is counted in orphanAgents below and reported. This is exactly the precedent refuterFanout already sets (an unresolved refuter goes to unrecoverableRefuterCount and is never bucketed into a unit, while the units that DID resolve in that run stay valid). A run-wide rule would not be conservative but destructive: real runs mix many named units with an occasional orphan (a 9-unit run is cited in refuterFanout.method), so one bad target could zero out the recoverable share and manufacture a verdict out of a corpus artefact. The missing-candidate hazard such a rule reaches for is caught locally instead, by dimension-coverage-gap: the unit's own finder set fails to cover the dimensions that were always-on for the whole window (code: ac + correctness; plan: coherence + architectural-fit — restraint is always-on today but shipped part-way through this window, so requiring it would flag pre-restraint units for an artefact of release timing), or the unit has a refuter for a dimension it has no finder for. The missing-VERDICT half is caught locally by unknown-disposition-above-determining, and only where it can actually bite: the walk skips any candidate whose severity is outside the tier's blocker set before it ever looks at that candidate's disposition, so an ungraded suggestion (or, at the default tier, an ungraded concern) leaves a unit non-determining rather than unrecoverable. Neither guesses which unit an orphan belonged to.
determiningFindingRank.orphanResidualRisk: The risk per-unit scoping accepts, stated rather than imputed: an orphan FINDER could in principle have belonged to a named unit whose dimension coverage nonetheless looks complete (e.g. an unlabeled retry), leaving that unit's candidate list silently short and its rank understated. orphanAgents.finders is the explicit UPPER BOUND on how many units could be understated that way. It is bounded and reported; it is never imputed, and it never invalidates a unit that did resolve. (orphanAgents.refuters reconciles exactly with refuterFanout.refuterCountsByUnit.unrecoverableRefuterCount above — the same 350 refuters, counted the same way.)
determiningFindingRank.tierCaveat: The tier is threaded through `context` at runtime and is embedded in NEITHER prompt, so it is NOT recoverable per unit. The headline figures use the DEFAULT blocker set (['blocking']); largeTier re-runs the identical walk with hasBlocking(findings,'large'), which widens blockers to ['blocking','concern']. Both are reported rather than a tier being guessed from an agent's model id. Widening the blocker set can only move a determining finding EARLIER in the same ranking, so largeTier's determining count and within-top counts are monotone above the default tier's — auditRankDoc asserts that directly.
determiningFindingRank.acTableCaveat: A SECOND outcome channel this measurement deliberately does not score. In code mode classifyOutcome routes a FAIL/PARTIAL AC table through acTableHasGap directly, never through finding severity or refutation, so a unit can have been `rework` with no gating finding at all. Counted here as its own diagnostic row; such units are NOT folded into nonDetermining. This phase's question is scoped to hasBlocking.

rule.basis: withinTop n=5, as a percentage of DETERMINING units; a cap is only supported when enough units were recoverable to speak to it at all.

determiningFindingRank.caveat: Every headline above is computed over RECOVERABLE units only, and the recoverable share is stated beside it: unrecoverable units contribute to no within-top-N numerator and to no percentOfDetermining / percentOfRecoverable denominator, and nothing is imputed for them (no default rank, no 'assume unrefuted', no 'assume the missing refuter agreed'). Phase 1's own bound carries forward: refuterFanout recovered a unit for only 64.6 % of refuters over this same window, which bounds how much of the corpus this section can speak to. Two further limits on the disposition half: the corpus cannot distinguish a refuter that crashed (which the live pipeline keeps as un-refuted) from one whose transcript is absent, so both are treated as `unknown` — conservative, and possibly divergent from what the pipeline actually did; and the run mix spans workflow-token-reduction phase 6, before which `suggestion` findings WERE refuted and after which they pass through ungraded, so a missing refuter for a suggestion is legitimate while a missing refuter for a gating finding is unknown. As with every other section here, no post-change corpus exists: this is an exact accounting of what the historical lane did, not a forecast.

gating.checkGatedBy: node scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs --check docs/token-baseline.json (recomputes over the real corpus; requires the sidecars, so it is run by hand, not by the harness)
gating.auditGatedBy: node scripts/measure-refuter-severity.mjs --audit docs/token-baseline.json, run by scripts/verify-token-report.sh section 7 — corpus-free arithmetic audit (determining + nonDetermining + unrecoverable === total; unrecoverableByReason sums to units.unrecoverable and every reason is in the closed vocabulary, with no run-wide reason admitted; rankHistogram sums to units.determining; withinTop is monotone in n and bounded by determining; every percentage re-derives from the doc's own counts; largeTier is monotone above the default tier; and capVerdict.verdict is RE-DERIVED via deriveCapVerdict/CAP_VERDICT_RULE), so the committed figures and the supports/kills conclusion are gated on any machine.

refuterModelTiering.question: Must the autonomous lane's refuters stay on Opus? Measured against an adjudicated finding corpus with false-negative and false-positive rates reported separately.

run.label: bounded-8x2x2
run.boundedRationale: A full 56-item x 2-tier x 2-replicate pass is 224 dispatches. At the means this run measured (533k tokens per Opus dispatch, 1.01M per Sonnet one), that is ~173M tokens. Spending that to decide a token-reduction question would be self-defeating, so the recorded run uses a stratified 8-item subset. The instrument supports the full pass.

notes: The corpus is DELIBERATELY WEIGHTED toward mechanically-true-not-a-defect (the class where the tiers diverged). The aggregate is therefore NOT a population estimate of production finding mix — quote the per-class rates.
False negatives and false positives have asymmetric cost and structurally different denominators. They are reported separately and are never averaged into an accuracy number.

Token figures here are VOLUME, not price. Re-tiering changes price-per-token, not token volume (the initial A/B measured Sonnet at 52.9k vs Opus 48.4k per refuter). Any cost conclusion is a price-per-token argument and must be labelled as such.
Historical `suggestion`-severity items are recorded but excluded from every headline rate: phase 6 landed NON_GATING_SEVERITIES = [suggestion], so no refuter is spawned for one again.

Ground truth is adjudicated against the PINNED TREE recorded in each item's groundTruth.adjudicatedAgainstCommit — the tree a replay run actually reads — not against the tree the historical refuter read. A finding that was real then and is fixed now is `stale-fact`/defect:false, because that is the correct answer for a refuter reading this tree.
